title: WPSS/2193/2014 of Laxmi Dutt Atwal Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No. 2193 of 2014
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Suresh Chnadra Bhatt,
Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. H.M. Raturi, Dy. A.G. alongwith
Mr. M.C. Tiwari, Addl. Dy. A.G. for the
State/respondent nos.
Heard learned counsel for the
parties.
By means of this petition, petitioner
seeks following reliefs:
(i) Issue a writ of certiorari to quash the
order dated 10.10.2014 and 30.1.2014
passed by respondent no.5.
(ii) Issue a writ order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding the
respondents not to recover the amount shown
in the impugned order passed by respondent
no.5 till the pendency of the writ petition.î
According to learned counsel for the
petitioner, petitioner was appointed as
Assistant Teacher in Education
Department w.e.f. 01.09.1979,
subsequently, he was promoted as
Lecturer. Petitioner ultimately retired on
31.03.2015 after availing benefit of
Government policy which provides that
any teacher who attains age of
superannuation during mid-academic-session would be permitted to continue
in service till end of academic session.
It is the case of petitioner that
Principal, G.I.C., Tankpur issued an
order dated 30.01.2014, whereby
recovery of Rs. 1,02,291/- was ordered.
Thereafter, Principal of the concerned
institution issued reminder on
10.10.2014 reiterating that the said
amount has been paid in excess to the
petitioner and he is liable to repay the

said amount. Thus feeling aggrieved
petitioner filed this writ petition.
Counter affidavit has been field by
the respondent no.5/Principal of the
concerned institution. Paragraph no.9 of
the said counter affidavit is extracted
below:
ìThat the contents of para 8 of the writ petition
are not admitted as stated in reply it is submitted
that the pay fixation of the petitioner has been done
on 16.12.2010 which was wrongly been fixed
therefore, when this mistake was came to knowledge
of the answering respondent department the same
was rectified. The pay increment has been done in
the case of the petitioner from 01.01.2006. That on
01.01.2010 by which the salary of the petitioner has
been fixed according to that the basic salary of the
petitioner was 25690/- which was later on rectified
by the petitioner and the same has been fixed as
24590/-. Prior to rectified the mistake therefore, the
petitioner has been paid the extra salary due to
mistake of the department therefore, the recovery
citation of the same has rightly been issued against
the petitioner by respondent no.5 by its letter dated
10.10.2014.î
Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that petitioner has never
misrepresented facts and he is not
responsible in any manner for excess
payment made to him. Learned counsel
for the petitioner further submits that
petitioner served the department since
1979 and he belongs to lower strata of
society.
Learned brief holder on the other
hand submits that pay scale of all
Government employees were revised in
terms of 6th Pay Commission report w.e.f.
01.01.2006 and due to mistake,
petitionerís basic pay was fixed as Rs.
25,690/- in place of Rs. 24,590/-.
Honíble Supreme Court in (2015)
(4) SCC 334 in the case of State of

Punjab and others Vs. Rafiq Masih
(White Washer) has held as under:
ì18. It is not possible to postulate all situations
of hardship, which would govern employees on the
issue of recovery, where payments have mistakenly
been made by the employer, in excess of their
entitlement. Be that as it may, based on the decisions
referred to herein above, we may, as a ready reference,
summarise the following few situations, wherein
recoveries by the employers, would be impermissible in
law:
 (i) Recovery from employees belonging to Class-III and Class-IV service (or Group 'C' and Group 'D'
service).
 (ii) Recovery from retired employees, or the
employees who are due to retire within one year, of the
order of recovery.
 (iii) Recovery from the employees, when the
excess payment has been made for a period in excess
of five years, before the order of recovery is issued.
 (iv) Recovery in cases where an employee has
wrongfully been required to discharge duties of a higher
post, and has been paid accordingly, even though he
should have rightfully been required to work against an
inferior post.
 (v) In any other case, where the Court arrives at
the conclusion, that recovery if made from the employee,
would be iniquitous or harsh or arbitrary to such an
extent, as would far outweigh the equitable balance of
the employer's right to recover.î
Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that petitioner has retired from
a Class III posts. He further submits that
excess amount which is sought to be
recovered was paid to petitioner for a
period in excess of 5 years and it was not
paid because of any misrepresentation or
fraud on the part of the petitioner but it
was paid due to mistake on the part of
the Authorities.
Admittedly, it is not the case of the
respondents that petitioner was
responsible for any excess payment
made to him. Thus, by applying the
principle laid down by Honíble Supreme

Court in case of State of Punjab Vs.
Rafiq Masih (supra), this Court has no
hesitation in holding that the
respondents are not justified in ordering
for recovery of Rs. 1,02,291/- from the
petitioner.
Accordingly, the writ petition is
allowed. Impugned orders dated
30.01.2014 & 10.10.2014 are quashed
and set aside.
No order as to costs.
(Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
27.07.2017
Mamta
